passages.provision_quote: Prohibits a governmental entity or any other person from knowingly or willfully keeping any list, record, or registry of: (1) privately owned firearms; or (2) the owners of firearms; with respect to Indiana consumers.
passages.note: The version he authored bans firearm registries and firearms merchant category codes, a privacy/financial dimension none of these rungs order.

passages.provision_quote: Amends the statute establishing the right of a member of: (1) the general assembly; (2) the professional staff of the general assembly; or (3) the Indiana lobby registration commission; to carry a handgun within the state capitol building and on the property of the state capitol complex by specifying that the right applies to any such member who is not prohibited under state or federal law from possessing a handgun.
passages.note: The capitol-carry provisions appear only in the enrolled digest, not in the introduced version he authored, and a carve-out for named officials in one building cannot separate the rungs on the loosening side.

rows.reasoning: Teshka authored HB 1084 (2024), whose introduced text "Prohibits a governmental entity or any other person from knowingly or willfully keeping any list, record, or registry of: (1) privately owned firearms; or (2) the owners of firearms" — a firearm-privacy measure, not the dimension these rungs order. The enrolled digest's right "to carry a handgun within the state capitol building and on the property of the state capitol complex" for named officials leans toward loosening but was added after the version he acted on, and a single building-specific carve-out cannot show he would "at most loosen rules on carrying" rather than "let adults carry a firearm without a permit."
